task: parse() only takes a bool for force_cdata. Make it selective, the way force_list already is. As well as True and False it should accept a tuple of element names, so only those elements get the dict form with the text under #text and the others stay plain strings: parse("data1data2data3", force_cdata=("b", "d")) gives {"a": {"b": {"#text": "data1"}, "c": "data2", "d": {"#text": "data3"}}}. Names match at any depth, an element with attributes keeps them as usual ({"@attr": "value", "#text": "data1"}), and an empty tuple behaves like False. It should also accept a callable, called as force_cdata(path, key, value) with the same path convention as the force_list callable, where key is the element name and value is its text, and a true result forces the dict form for that element. True and False keep working exactly as they do now.
